entries.note: The claim combines a causal account of semiconductor sales with an explicitly small likelihood of LLM transformation.

entries.test: Whether a reduction below the stated quarterly spending level by these hyperscalers is followed by a substantial contraction in semiconductor demand and sales.
entries.note: The supercycle metaphor has a plain economic reading in context.

entries.test: Public customer spending and cloud revenue disclosures would show whether these GPUs generate revenue from other customers and whether the two labs account for at least 20% of the named providers' cloud revenues.
entries.note: An explicitly labeled numerical estimate remains checkable.

entries.test: Funding records and infrastructure spending attributable to the two labs would establish their combined funding and cost, excluding Oracle's stated Stargate buildout.
entries.note: The estimate specifies which additional infrastructure costs it includes and excludes.
The central assertion assigns an exclusive hidden purpose to the companies' separate existence. It also includes a judgment about wasted spending.
Both the revenue share and its persistence are expressly hedged.
“Appears to be” makes this a tentative assessment of capex outcomes.

entries.test: Meta's public advertising experiments, revenue attribution analyses and financial disclosures would show whether GPU-supported AI produces material incremental advertising revenue.
entries.note: “Meaningful” permits a plain reading of a material commercial contribution.

entries.test: The suppliers' sales breakdowns, hyperscaler purchases and evidence of underlying compute utilization would show whether speculative hyperscaler expansion accounts for their record sales.
entries.note: Evaluative adjectives accompany a concrete claim about the source of sales.

entries.test: Public compute procurement records, data center construction timelines and utilization after completion would test the customer concentration and claimed construction-delay explanation.
entries.note: The claim asserts both an absence of other major customers and an exclusive causal explanation.
“Waste” and “suck” express judgments of worth without an agreed test.

entries.test: Representative customer sentiment, product revenue disclosures and evidence connecting GitHub Copilot adoption to compute subsidies would test the assertion.
entries.note: “These products” refers to the preceding list, whereas the normalization broadens this to big tech's AI products generally. The subsidy explanation is causal.

entries.test: Durable commercial success or abandonment of LLM technology for reliable autonomous work would test the prediction that the technology is doomed.
entries.note: The source names Pichai, Jassy, Nadella and Zuckerberg; the normalization broadens this to industry leaders. “Doomed” supplies a future outcome alongside present criticisms.
This judges the sufficiency of an argument; it does not predict that autonomous tools will never emerge.
The characterization of the report as marketing and its sources as questionable is an evaluative verdict.
The assertion concerns designers' intentions, rather than measurable engagement or productivity effects.
The claim attributes fantasies, private aims and deliberate fear-based manipulation to agent makers.
“Conning” expresses his judgment about what deserves to be called autonomous.

entries.test: Public studies of affected tech workers' hours and comparable output before and after mandated AI adoption would test whether work doubled without increased output.
entries.note: The numerical comparison is testable despite its polemical setting.
Both assertions are qualified as appearances rather than firm conclusions.

entries.test: Public comparisons of model deployment costs with labor costs, documented worker replacement and provider margins would test the economic assertions.
entries.note: The opening worth judgment is subjective, but the compound claim also makes firm factual assertions about costs, replacement and profitability.
“The jig is up” supplies no definite failure event or outcome.

entries.test: Public contracts and sustained utilization sufficient to support the planned data center capacity would contradict the prediction of permanently insufficient demand.
entries.note: The following sentence qualifies this as insufficient demand unless the technology changes substantially and soon. The normalization turns that contextual claim into an absolute absence of demand.

entries.test: Public compute contracts, financing requirements, customer pricing protests and investment or IPO valuations would test the commitments and accompanying market claims.
entries.note: The market language has a concrete valuation reading in the surrounding IPO discussion.

entries.test: Major investment losses, bankruptcies or financial disruptions accompanying the end of the current AI investment era would test the predicted financial carnage.
entries.note: “I expect” is a firm expectation. The normalization drops the stated condition for avoidability; that counterfactual component cannot itself be publicly settled.
